corr.color.why:
The color a camera records depends on the light (sun, cloud, lamp), the camera and its automatic settings. Two photos of the same seed can give different colors.

With a card of known colors in the photo, each photo is brought to the real colors of the card (or to those of a reference photo), so colors can be compared across photos, days, devices and places.

For it to work: the whole card in the photo, no glare or shadows on it, and each patch at least about 20 px. It may be rotated. If you only have a white or gray card, the white balance (the overall tint of the light) is corrected, not each color.
corr.distortion.bad_grid: Columns and rows must be integers.
corr.distortion.failed: Calibration failed: corners found in {used} of {total} images (at least 3 needed).
corr.distortion.short: So that size does not depend on where the object falls in the photo
corr.distortion.why:
Lenses, especially wide-angle and phone lenses, bend the image: straight lines near the edges look curved and the same object looks larger or smaller depending on where it falls in the photo.

Uncorrected, a seed near the edge can measure several % differently from the same seed in the center. After correction, size and shape do not depend on position.

Calibrate once per camera, lens and zoom, with 10–20 photos of a chessboard from different angles. If you change camera, lens or zoom, calibrate again.
corr.intro: Optional. Applied in memory, in this order, whenever an image is opened.
corr.not_applied.color: Color: the card was not found in this photo (or it is not set up).

corr.not_applied.perspective: Perspective: the 4 ArUco markers were not found in this photo.
corr.perspective.help: Needs 4 ArUco markers (DICT_4X4_50) with IDs 0 top-left, 1 top-right, 2 bottom-right, 3 bottom-left. The image is straightened without stretching. If you enter the real distances between marker centers, the scale (mm/px) is also computed for each image.
corr.perspective.short: To straighten photos taken slightly at an angle and get each photo's scale
corr.perspective.use_scale: Use as scale for each image
corr.perspective.why:
If the camera is not exactly parallel to the surface, the photo is in perspective: farther things look smaller and rectangles look like trapezoids.

With 4 ArUco markers at the corners, the photo is straightened. If you also enter the real distance between the markers, each photo gets its own scale (mm/px), even if the camera height changes slightly between photos.

The markers must be fully visible in every photo; if one is missing, that photo is not analyzed (so corrected and uncorrected photos are never mixed).

param.distances.measure.label: Measure
param.distances.measure.tip: Edge to edge along the line between centers: the free space between both objects in that direction. Closest point: the minimum gap between their outlines. Center to center: between their centroids. The Clark-Evans index always uses centers: R < 1 clustered, R ≈ 1 random, R > 1 evenly spaced (95 % test).
param.distances.neighbors.label: Neighbors
param.distances.neighbors.tip: Nearest: each object with its k closest neighbors. Voronoi network: each object with the ones directly around it (no need to choose how many).
param.distances.touching.label: Objects touch
param.image_color.n_colors.label: Number of colors
param.image_color.n_colors.tip: How many dominant colors to find (KMeans). Excluded areas are ignored; if there is an analysis area, only that area is used.
param.objects.color_mode.label: Colors
param.objects.color_mode.tip: Of each object: each object gets its own dominant colors. All together: one shared palette for the photo and the % of each color in each object (makes objects comparable).

param.objects.measure_count.label: Count

param.objects.measure_shape.label: Shape

workres.full: Full photo (may need a lot of memory)
workres.help:
Corrections (lens, ArUco, color card) are made on the full photo. Then, if the photo is larger than this size, it is reduced for analysis, so a 200 MP photo does not need 10 GB of memory.

The scale is adjusted automatically, so measurements in mm do not change; only very fine detail is lost. Photos smaller than the chosen size are analyzed in full.

50 MP is enough for seeds and leaves in almost every setup.
